name: Shallowing — Foreskin / Glans Dipping Glide
summary: Male variant of Shallowing. Instead of going deep, the foreskin (or a slick grip) glides up and down over the glans, covering and uncovering the head on each slow pass and cycling through the most sensitive surface.
detailed_description: Female Shallowing cycles through the entrance zone instead of going deep. The male analogue keeps stimulation at the head: the foreskin or a lubricated hand slides up to sheath the glans, then back to expose it, repeating shallow up/down passes. For circumcised anatomy the same effect comes from a slick grip gliding over the corona without long full-length strokes. The repeated covering/uncovering keeps attention on the richly nerved head rather than the shaft.
stepwise_structure: 1. Use lube so the glide stays smooth.
2. Slide the foreskin (or a slick grip) up to cover the glans.
3. Draw it back down to uncover the head.
4. Repeat slow, shallow up/down passes over the head and corona.
5. Keep the range short—dwell on the head rather than the whole shaft.
safety_notes: Use enough lube so covering/uncovering never tugs uncomfortably.
Keep the head exposed gently; don't force a tight foreskin.
